review_rounds.regression_proof: with only the three edited source files stashed, exactly the 6 new tests fail (45 pass); all 51 pass after the fix — recorded in commands.log

Stale results after replace/cancel canno.detail: Every inbound WorkerMessage is validated then admitted through MessageAuthority (generation -> document_sha256 -> run_key -> job registration -> strictly increasing seq) before it can touch state; rejected messages mutate nothing and return a named code. Tests: 'a stale-generation message is rejected and changes nothing' (revision/snapshot unchanged), 'old document hash is rejected as stale_document', 'old run_key is rejected as stale_run on a new run of the same file', 'unknown job, replayed seq and late chunks to terminal jobs are rejected' (terminal_job), 'a stale check_terminal cannot flip a live check' (failure never becomes agreement), 'cancel preserves completed evidence and kills the old generation' (post-cancel events rejected, completed occurrences still in the view), and 'replace: clearing -> validating_file, old generation fully dead' (generation bumps BEFORE teardown; the stale chunk's occurrence ids are asserted absent from the new view — they cannot render). SessionStore tests show the same at the presentation layer: stale ingestions return rejections only and the view never changes.

256-occurrence chunks and two unacked ca.detail: Bound enforced in both directions on the real wire shape. Producer side: 'ChunkSender emits <=256-occurrence chunks and holds at two unacked' — 512 occurrences emit as exactly 256+256, a third sendNext returns null while two are unacknowledged, and acknowledge(seq) reopens the window (acks are capacity, never success). Receiver side: 'malformed inbound is rejected before admission' — a 257-occurrence chunk fails contract validation (schema payload.occurrences maxItems=256) as 'malformed' before admission; 'inbound: a third chunk while two are unacknowledged is a protocol violation' — InboundWindow counts accepted-minus-delivered-acks per check and the flood kills only the offending job's check with reason protocol; 'delivered acks reopen the window' — an ack counts only once drained from the coordinator outbox, so the bound holds on the receive side too.

cancelled/partial/failed differ.detail: computeRunStatus implements the lifecycle rule exactly and tests pin each outcome as a distinct terminal fileState plus snapshot run.status: 'cancelled, partial and failed are distinct outcomes' (three separate runs), 'a fully completed run is complete', 'partial run: one page fails, the completed page keeps its results' (I17 — sibling retained ids intact), 'failed run: nothing completed and at least one failure', 'unsupported-only run is partial, not failed and not complete', 'queued work cancelled by the user receives a terminal cancelled result' (never-queued checks still settle terminal), and 'run deadline watchdog terminalizes live checks as timeout'. Unsupported/cancelled/timeout/failed/skipped are all named terminal check statuses with schema CheckResult records.

empty success not retried.detail: Test 'empty success is completed, never retried (acceptance criterion)': a check_terminal reporting completed with zero occurrences terminalizes as completed with retained_occurrence_ids=[] — status is completed (not skipped), no retry is dispatched (outbox has no second dispatch intent), and a second check_terminal for the same check is rejected terminal_job. Retry is reserved for transient worker_crash-class reasons only ('worker_crash is retried once on a fresh job identity', 'the retry budget is one', 'no automatic retry on cancel/encrypted/unsupported/integrity/timeout', 'a crash beyond the remaining run budget is not retried').

UI cancellation target of 100 ms and ter.detail: Measured on the real coordinator cancel path with the real clock (performance.now) and real setTimeout arming inside the node:test process: test 'cancel order: visible cancelled state precedes teardown' asserts the cancelled fileState is observable (revision bump, listener fired) before any teardown verb runs; 'cancel timing: UI update under 100 ms, teardown under 500 ms (measured)' asserts receipt.uiMs < 100 and receipt.teardownMs < 500 on the CancelReceipt returned by requestCancel — measured ~30 ms total in this environment. 'cancel preserves completed evidence and kills the old generation' asserts old-generation events are unreachable afterwards. Honest scope note: this is an in-process integration measurement of the coordinator's cancel path — no browser worker embedder exists in this checkout (it arrives with the reader/viewer tasks), so the numbers are coordinator-observed, not device-measured browser timings. The CancelReceipt interface is designed so the browser harness re-measures the same boundaries once integrated.

limitations: The 100 ms / 500 ms cancellation targets are measured in-process on the real coordinator with real timers inside node:test; a browser-integrated measurement needs the worker embedder that lands in a later task (T15+). The measured values (~30 ms total) are coordinator-observed, not browser device timings.
